paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following text. Choose the best word(s) for each numbered blank and mark A, B, C or D on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文字。为每个编号的空白处选择最佳的单词，并在答题卡上标记 A、B、C 或 D。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Most of us strive for self-respect — to see ourselves in a positive light, to be 1 of who we are. Any comments or experiences that undermine those feelings of self-worth can be uncomfortable and it’s only 2 to want to avoid them. But the thing is, 3 your self-worth really is being undermined is, to a large degree, subjective. Much of it comes down to your 4 of what someone said or did.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们大多数人都努力争取自尊——以积极的眼光看待自己，为自己感到自豪。任何破坏自我价值感的评论或经历都会让人感到不舒服，想要避免它们是很自然的。但问题是，你的自我价值是否真的受到损害在很大程度上是主观的。这很大程度上取决于你对某人所说或所做的看法。

paragraphs.sourceText: When you take things personally, you’re interpreting these situations as saying something significant and negative about you as a person. Say your boss picks holes in your sales report, and you come away feeling like this means she thinks you’re a 5 member of staff. Or, two of your friends cancel your 6 get-together at the pub and you interpret this as meaning they’re bored of you. Psychologists have a 7 for this way of thinking: personalisation.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当你把事情看成是针对你个人的时候，你就会把这些情况解释为对你这个人的一些重要和负面的影响。假设你的老板在你的销售报告中发现了漏洞，你离开时会觉得这意味着她认为你是一个糟糕的员工。或者，您的两个朋友取消了您计划的酒吧聚会，您将此解释为他们对您感到厌倦。心理学家对这种思维方式有一个术语：个性化。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the 8 is that your boss might view you very highly. It’s just you made some 9 in the report and she wanted to point these out so that you do better next time. 10 , in the case of your friends cancelling, perhaps they both felt unwell that weekend or they just 11 their minds.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但现实情况是，你的老板可能对你评价很高。只是你在报告中犯了一些错误，她想指出这些错误，以便你下次做得更好。同样，如果您的朋友取消预订，也许他们那个周末都感觉不舒服，或者只是改变了主意。

paragraphs.sourceText: In both 12 — and others that we all experience — there’s another 13 at work that psychologists call mind reading. This is when you assume to know what other people are thinking about you, when you can’t really know without 14 them directly.
paragraphs.translationZh: 在这两个例子以及我们都经历过的其他例子中，还有另一个过程在起作用，心理学家称之为“读心术”。这是当你假设知道其他人对你的想法时，如果不直接询问他们就无法真正知道。

paragraphs.sourceText: One simple way to avoid 15 personalisation and mind reading is to challenge your negative assumptions of what’s 16 . When you find yourself taking a situation personally, try to think of other interpretations that are less focused on you — especially in the sense of saying anything deep or 17 about you.
paragraphs.translationZh: 避免陷入个性化和读心术的一种简单方法是挑战你对所发生事情的负面假设。当你发现自己把某种情况看成是针对你个人的时候，试着想一些不那么关注你的其他解释——尤其是在谈论任何关于你的深刻或基本的事情的意义上。

paragraphs.sourceText: When you do this, it might help to try to put yourself in other people’s shoes. The fact your boss took the time to give you 18 at all means they care enough to want to help you 19 . When it comes to your friends — maybe it’s because your friendship is so 20 that they felt able to cancel at late notice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当你这样做时，尝试设身处地为别人着想可能会有所帮助。事实上，你的老板花时间给你反馈，这意味着他们非常关心你，想要帮助你改进。当谈到你的朋友时——也许是因为你们的友谊如此深厚，以至于他们觉得可以在很晚的情况下取消。

paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following four texts. Answer the questions after each text by choosing A, B, C or D. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (40 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读下面四篇课文。选择 A、B、C 或 D 来回答每篇课文后的问题。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （40分）

paragraphs.sourceText: Ask people about public libraries and a certain image springs to mind: dusty, old-fashioned, the sort of place you enjoyed as a child but, rather like a British seaside town, would you go there now? And anyway — aren’t they all closing?
paragraphs.translationZh: 当向人们询问公共图书馆时，脑海中浮现出这样的画面：尘土飞扬、老式的、你小时候喜欢的那种地方，但就像英国的海滨小镇一样，你现在会去那里吗？无论如何——他们不是都关门了吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: The reality is startlingly different, as I discovered when the culture department commissioned me to conduct an independent review of English public libraries, published yesterday. As I visited libraries up and down the country, I was surprised to learn there are more than twice the number of libraries (2,892) as there are branches of McDonald’s.
paragraphs.translationZh: 现实却截然不同，当文化部门委托我对昨天发表的英国公共图书馆进行独立审查时，我发现了这一点。当我参观全国各地的图书馆时，我惊讶地发现图书馆的数量（2,892 个）是麦当劳分店的两倍多。

paragraphs.sourceText: Enter any one of them and you will find a hive of activity. While books are, and should always be, at the heart of any library, a multitude of other services are offered: employment advice, language classes or digital access and support.
paragraphs.translationZh: 输入其中任何一个，您都会发现一片活跃的景象。虽然书籍是而且应该永远是任何图书馆的核心，但图书馆还提供多种其他服务：就业建议、语言课程或数字访问和支持。

paragraphs.sourceText: There are libraries with business and intellectual property centres, which can help business owners and entrepreneurs. Many have nurses on site to carry out basic health checks, with a link to the GP’s surgery. There are libraries where young people can borrow a Fifa-standard football free.
paragraphs.translationZh: 有些图书馆设有商业和知识产权中心，可以为企业主和企业家提供帮助。许多医院都有护士在现场进行基本的健康检查，并与全科医生的手术联系起来。年轻人可以在图书馆免费借用国际足联标准的足球。

paragraphs.sourceText: In return for all of this, you’ll be asked for precisely nothing. There will be no charge and you will never be asked to justify or explain yourself; you will simply be welcomed in, offered help if you need it, and left alone if you do not. There is no other institution, public or private, that can say the same. Yet still our libraries are often overlooked and underappreciated. There is an overall decline in visits and many are struggling as local authorities come under continued financial pressure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 作为这一切的回报，你不会被要求任何东西。不会收取任何费用，也不会要求您为自己辩护或解释；我们只会欢迎您进来，并在您需要时提供帮助，如果您不需要则独自一人。没有其他机构，无论是公立还是私立，可以说同样的话。然而，我们的图书馆仍然经常被忽视和低估。由于地方当局面临持续的财政压力，游客数量总体下降，许多人陷入困境。

paragraphs.sourceText: The number of libraries that have closed since 2010 is disputed. An annual survey by the Chartered Institute of Public Finance and Accountancy puts it at nearly 800 across the UK; official statistics held by the Arts Council record 230 in England. It is, of course, 230 libraries too many. So if we are to protect our libraries for future generations, we must raise awareness of them and the work they do.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自 2010 年以来关闭的图书馆数量存在争议。英国特许公共财政与会计学会的一项年度调查显示，英国各地的这一数字接近 800；英国艺术理事会的官方统计记录为230个。当然，230 个库太多了。因此，如果我们要为子孙后代保护我们的图书馆，我们就必须提高对它们及其所做工作的认识。

paragraphs.sourceText: The review recommends a national branding campaign to give libraries a stronger physical presence, the reintroduction of a scheme to enable members to use their card in any library in the country, and automatic memberships for children. If we don’t use them, we will end up losing them. And for those who haven’t been to a library for some time, they may be surprised by what they find.
paragraphs.translationZh: 审查建议开展全国品牌宣传活动，以增强图书馆的实体存在，重新引入一项计划，使会员能够在全国任何图书馆使用他们的卡，并为儿童提供自动会员资格。如果我们不使用它们，我们最终就会失去它们。对于那些已经有一段时间没有去过图书馆的人来说，他们可能会对自己的发现感到惊讶。

paragraphs.sourceText: According to our research, around one in five workers in the UK talk to AI like a friend, looking for guidance on personal and professional problems. Our data shows that engaging with AI like this can leave us feeling heard and less isolated. But, with this newfound connection, many of us share sensitive, sometimes highly confidential information, even though over a third of people don’t realise that AI platforms may not be very good at keeping our secrets...secret.
paragraphs.translationZh: 根据我们的研究，英国大约五分之一的员工像朋友一样与人工智能交谈，寻求有关个人和职业问题的指导。我们的数据表明，像这样与人工智能互动可以让我们感到被倾听，并且减少孤立感。但是，通过这种新发现的联系，我们中的许多人共享敏感的、有时是高度机密的信息，尽管超过三分之一的人没有意识到人工智能平台可能不太擅长保守我们的秘密……秘密。

paragraphs.sourceText: For businesses, the implications are worrying. Consider Microsoft Copilot, for example. It grants Microsoft broad rights to the data inputted or outputted by any user — rights to use this data in any way it sees fit; it can even share it with third parties. This means that any sensitive business information could potentially be exposed to the world. Employers are taking note and taking action. According to our research, 25% have decided to either outright ban AI or regulate its use within their organisations. But even with these policies in place, some employees choose to break the rules. They have their reasons — around 63% of them report that using AI increases their productivity, and some even feel AI offers more help than their human colleagues.
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于企业来说，其影响令人担忧。以 Microsoft Copilot 为例。它授予微软对任何用户输入或输出的数据的广泛权利——以任何它认为合适的方式使用这些数据的权利；它甚至可以与第三方共享。这意味着任何敏感的商业信息都有可能暴露给全世界。雇主们正在关注并采取行动。根据我们的研究，25% 的人决定要么彻底禁止人工智能，要么在组织内规范人工智能的使用。但即使制定了这些政策，一些员工还是选择违反规则。他们有自己的理由——大约 63% 的人表示，使用人工智能提高了他们的工作效率，有些人甚至认为人工智能比人类同事提供了更多帮助。

paragraphs.sourceText: The situation presents a delicate balance between leveraging AI for its productivity gains and risking confidential data exposure. Employers need to manage AI tools with the same level of care as any other form of data sharing or storage. There’s also a knowledge gap that needs to be addressed — 40% of individuals surveyed are unsure about who retains ownership over the content produced by AI. By instilling best practices in AI engagement and creating policies that evolve with the technology, businesses can positively shift the AI landscape.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种情况在利用人工智能提高生产力和冒机密数据泄露风险之间呈现出微妙的平衡。雇主需要像管理任何其他形式的数据共享或存储一样谨慎地管理人工智能工具。还有一个知识差距需要解决——40% 的受访者不确定谁拥有人工智能生成的内容的所有权。通过灌输人工智能参与的最佳实践并制定随技术发展而发展的政策，企业可以积极改变人工智能格局。

paragraphs.sourceText: With AI’s potential to simplify our professional lives, do the admin and enhance the work experience, it’s up to us to navigate its usage cautiously so it supports us without compromising our privacy. There’s no need to back away from progress, as long as we’re equipped with the knowledge and tools to make sure AI remains a friend. And this is where the challenge lies. There are so many products out there, being promoted with huge advertising and marketing budgets, that it’s easy to fall victim. But by building a culture of digital responsibility within our businesses, we can create a future where AI can help us without spilling the beans.
paragraphs.translationZh: 人工智能有潜力简化我们的职业生活、进行管理并增强工作体验，因此我们需要谨慎地使用它，以便它在不损害我们隐私的情况下为我们提供支持。只要我们配备了知识和工具来确保人工智能仍然是我们的朋友，就没有必要放弃进步。这就是挑战所在。市场上有如此多的产品，并以巨额广告和营销预算进行推广，因此很容易成为受害者。但通过在我们的企业内部建立数字责任文化，我们可以创造一个人工智能可以在不泄露秘密的情况下帮助我们的未来。

paragraphs.sourceText: Since the 2008 launch of the high-speed rail network between Rome and Milan, trains have become the preferred means of travel across Italy for locals and tourists alike. Fast trains can cover the 500km between the two cities in three hours. The network also connects Naples, Bologna, Florence and Turin. In many cases, it is the best option — in terms of travel time and cost — for both leisure and business travellers.
paragraphs.translationZh: 自2008年罗马和米兰之间的高铁网络开通以来，火车已成为当地人和游客穿越意大利的首选交通工具。快速列车可以在三个小时内覆盖两个城市之间的 500 公里。该网络还连接那不勒斯、博洛尼亚、佛罗伦萨和都灵。在许多情况下，无论是对于休闲旅客还是商务旅客来说，就旅行时间和成本而言，它都是最佳选择。

paragraphs.sourceText: This is why the recent severe delays caused by numerous maintenance works have thrown the rail industry into chaos at a time when most people head on holiday, which matters for business in a country where tourism accounts for 10 percent of GDP.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这就是为什么最近在大多数人去度假的时候，大量维修工程造成的严重延误让铁路行业陷入混乱，这对于一个旅游业占GDP 10%的国家的商业至关重要。

paragraphs.sourceText: Disruptions have become increasingly frequent with train delays now a fixture in Italian media coverage. Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane, the publicly controlled group that owns train operator Trenitalia and the national train network RFI, said 23 percent of all high-speed trains it operated were late in 2023.
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着火车晚点成为意大利媒体报道的焦点，列车延误变得越来越频繁。 Ferrovie dello Stato Italiane 是一家公共控股集团，拥有火车运营商 Trenitalia 和国家铁路网络 RFI，该集团表示，其运营的所有高速列车中有 23% 到 2023 年晚点。

paragraphs.sourceText: The huge improvements in Italy’s obsolete infrastructure partly explained the disruption, said Ferrovie. RFI, the network operator, is the single largest European recovery fund beneficiary with planned investments of €24bn by 2026. Ferrovie will invest a total of €124bn in infrastructure over the next 10 years.
paragraphs.translationZh: 费罗维说，意大利陈旧基础设施的巨大改进在一定程度上解释了这种破坏。网络运营商 RFI 是欧洲最大的复苏基金受益者，计划到 2026 年投资 240 亿欧元。Ferrovie 将在未来 10 年在基础设施领域投资总计 1,240 亿欧元。

paragraphs.sourceText: But lack of capacity is another problem. Transport economist Andrea Giuricin said the planned investments would bring improvements but disruptions in the meantime were inevitable. “We have a mixed system, there is no spare capacity and as soon as there’s a hiccup on the line, the situation becomes highly complex,” he said. A mixed system means that high-speed trains must travel on the regular tracks on certain routes or when passing through large cities. If there’s congestion or, for example, a local train breaks down, the entire high-speed network is affected.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但能力不足是另一个问题。交通经济学家 Andrea Giuricin 表示，计划中的投资将带来改善，但同时造成的干扰是不可避免的。 “我们有一个混合系统，没有闲置产能，一旦生产线出现问题，情况就会变得非常复杂，”他说。混合系统意味着高速列车在某些路线或经过大城市时必须在常规轨道上行驶。如果出现拥堵，或者当地火车发生故障，整个高速网络都会受到影响。

paragraphs.sourceText: One of the most important changes the upgrades will bring is the segregation of the high-speed line from the regular one in certain urban centres through the construction of underground rail links.
paragraphs.translationZh: 升级带来的最重要的变化之一是通过建设地下铁路将某些城市中心的高速线路与普通线路分开。

paragraphs.sourceText: Improvements will also come from the high-density technology and satellite signalling that RFI has been investing in for years, say experts. It will allow for a reduction of the distance between high-speed trains travelling on the same line at any given time, which should mean a significant increase in capacity and traffic fluidity, according to Giuricin.
paragraphs.translationZh: 专家表示，RFI 多年来投资的高密度技术和卫星信号也将带来改进。朱里辛表示，这将减少在任何特定时间在同一条线路上行驶的高速列车之间的距离，这意味着容量和交通流动性的显着增加。

paragraphs.sourceText: In 2023, Chicago lost one of its most beloved street festivals. The Silver Room Block Party, staged by Hyde Park community leader Eric Williams, announced it would not return in 2024. What began as a small neighborhood gathering blossomed into a massive cultural event, welcoming tens of thousands of people each year over nearly two decades before abruptly shutting down.
paragraphs.translationZh: 2023 年，芝加哥失去了最受欢迎的街头节日之一。由海德公园社区领袖埃里克·威廉姆斯 (Eric Williams) 举办的银屋街区派对 (Silver Room Block Party) 宣布，该活动将不会在 2024 年回归。最初的小型社区聚会后来发展成为一场大型文化活动，近二十年来每年都会接待数万人，然后突然关闭。

paragraphs.sourceText: Williams pointed to rising production costs and declining attendee donations as primary reasons the Silver Room Block Party could not continue, highlighting a reality that all street festival organizers face right now. The cost of producing a street festival in Chicago has skyrocketed. Security, entertainment, portable restrooms, insurance and even basics such as fencing and staffing have all become significantly more expensive. At the same time, donations at festival gates have dropped dramatically.
paragraphs.translationZh: 威廉姆斯指出，制作成本上升和参与者捐款减少是银屋街区派对无法继续的主要原因，强调了所有街头节日组织者目前面临的现实。芝加哥举办街头音乐节的成本飙升。安全、娱乐、便携式卫生间、保险，甚至栅栏和人员配备等基本设施都变得更加昂贵。与此同时，节日门口的捐款急剧下降。

paragraphs.sourceText: Chicago’s summer festivals are about more than just entertainment; they are economic engines that directly benefit the neighborhoods they’re in and the city of Chicago as whole. Street festivals drive foot traffic to local businesses and foster the kind of cultural vibrancy that makes our city special.
paragraphs.translationZh: 芝加哥的夏季节日不仅仅在于娱乐，还在于娱乐。他们是经济引擎，直接造福于他们所在的社区和整个芝加哥市。街头节日带动了当地企业的人流量，并培养了使我们的城市与众不同的文化活力。

paragraphs.sourceText: We often hear people ask why we solicit donations at our entry points, especially when the city’s largest festivals like the Chicago Jazz Festival do not request donations. The fact is, unlike those large, city-produced music festivals, your neighborhood street festivals receive no city funding and rely on a combination of sponsorships, vendor fees and gate donations to cover their costs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们经常听到人们问我们为什么在入口处募集捐款，特别是当芝加哥爵士音乐节等该市最大的节日不要求捐款时。事实上，与那些大型的、城市举办的音乐节不同，你家附近的街头音乐节没有得到城市的资助，而是依靠赞助、供应商费用和门票捐赠来支付费用。

paragraphs.sourceText: Wicker Park Fest has long been one of Chicago’s most anticipated summer festivals, drawing upward of 70,000 attendees for a full weekend of live indie music, local art, small business vendors and, most importantly, community connection. In 2024, Wicker Park Fest saw record-breaking attendance. Despite the turnout, gate donations reached their lowest point in our history. This year, we’ve been forced to scale back the footprint of the fest. We are eliminating a stage, booking fewer performers and making additional cuts to reduce our costs, all while striving to keep the festival as vibrant as ever, as supportive of local artists and businesses, and as true to Wicker Park’s unique spirit and reputation as festgoers have come to expect.
paragraphs.translationZh: 柳条公园音乐节长期以来一直是芝加哥最受期待的夏季音乐节之一，吸引了超过 70,000 名参与者参加整个周末的现场独立音乐、当地艺术、小企业摊贩以及最重要的社区联系。 2024 年，柳条公园节的出席人数打破了纪录。尽管投票率很高，但门票捐款却达到了我们历史上的最低点。今年，我们被迫缩减了节日的规模。我们正在取消一个舞台，减少预订表演者，并进行额外削减以降低成本，同时努力使音乐节一如既往地充满活力，支持当地艺术家和企业，并忠实于威克公园独特的精神和声誉，正如音乐节观众所期望的那样。

paragraphs.sourceText: This summer, as you enjoy your favorite neighborhood street festival, I hope you’ll remember that they exist because of community support. A thriving summer festival season doesn’t happen by accident; it happens when we all chip in.
paragraphs.translationZh: 今年夏天，当您享受您最喜欢的邻里街头节日时，我希望您会记住它们的存在是因为社区的支持。暑期的热闹并非偶然。当我们大家都参与进来时，就会发生这种情况。

paragraphs.sourceText: Read the following text and match each of the numbered items in the left column to its corresponding information in the right column. There are two extra choices in the right column. Mark your answers on the ANSWER SHEET. (10 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 阅读以下文本，并将左栏中的每个编号项目与右栏中的相应信息相匹配。右栏中有两个额外的选项。在答题卡上标记您的答案。 （10分）

paragraphs.sourceText: In an effort to support restoration programmes, specialists are developing supplies of seeds and seedlings, maintaining gene banks and sequencing the genomes of indigenous trees and other crops. Their work deals with one of the problems that could block major restoration efforts in different parts of the world.
paragraphs.translationZh: 为了支持恢复计划，专家们正在开发种子和幼苗的供应，维护基因库并对本土树木和其他作物的基因组进行测序。他们的工作解决了可能阻碍世界各地重大修复工作的问题之一。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Where’s the planting material going to come from? That’s one big bottleneck,” says genetic-resources specialist Ramni Jamnadass.
paragraphs.translationZh: “种植材料从哪里来？这是一个很大的瓶颈，”遗传资源专家拉姆尼·贾姆纳德斯 (Ramni Jamnadass) 说。

paragraphs.sourceText: Asia is arguably the region most neglected by global efforts to increase diversity in restoration and to study native species. Christopher Kettle, Biodiversity International’s director for forest genetic resources and restoration in Rome, says that the need for infrastructure — things such as mechanisms for collecting and storing seeds, and nurseries to raise seedlings — might be most desperate here because many trees are ‘masting’ species, which don’t produce seeds every year. People need to be ready. “Otherwise, you miss the boat, you lose all the seed and you’ve got to wait another seven years,” says Kettle. “This is a really, really critical issue for restoration in Southeast Asia, because many of the most important timber species and tree species — the ones that will lock up the most carbon — they’re all masting species.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 亚洲可以说是全球在增加恢复多样性和研究本土物种的努力中最被忽视的地区。国际生物多样性组织驻罗马森林遗传资源和恢复主任克里斯托弗·凯特尔 (Christopher Kettle) 表示，这里对基础设施的需求可能最为迫切，例如收集和储存种子的机制以及培育幼苗的苗圃等，因为许多树木都是“肥大”树种，它们不会每年产生种子。人们需要做好准备。 “否则，你就会错失良机，失去所有种子，还得再等七年，”凯特尔说。 “这对东南亚的恢复来说是一个非常非常关键的问题，因为许多最重要的木材树种和树种——那些能够锁住最多碳的树种——它们都是桅杆树种。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Climate change is a driving factor in the push to restore forests, but it also raises questions, such as where trees can thrive in the future. Climate change is also expected to alter relationships between trees, insects, diseases and other forest species. “Insects that today are a minor problem may become a major problem if they can produce three or four generations in a year,” says forest ecologist John Stanturf. This remains a significant knowledge gap. “We know enough to know that this is a concern, but we don’t know enough about how to respond to it yet. That’s a great area to be doing research.” So is soil, says Cindy Prescott, a forest ecologist at the University of British Columbia in Vancouver. “If you don’t look at the soil at the start, you can spend a lot of money and time putting in species that aren’t going to survive there.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 气候变化是推动森林恢复的一个驱动因素，但它也提出了一些问题，例如未来树木可以在哪里茁壮成长。气候变化预计也会改变树木、昆虫、疾病和其他森林物种之间的关系。森林生态学家约翰·斯坦特夫（John Stanturf）说：“今天的小问题昆虫如果一年能产生三到四代，可能会成为大问题。”这仍然是一个重大的知识差距。 “我们足够了解这是一个令人担忧的问题，但我们还不知道如何应对它。这是一个值得研究的重要领域。”温哥华不列颠哥伦比亚大学的森林生态学家辛迪·普雷斯科特说，土壤也是如此。 “如果你一开始就不关注土壤，你可能会花费大量金钱和时间来种植那些无法在那里生存的物种。”

paragraphs.sourceText: With so much research left to do, leaders in the field have been doing some soul-searching, and acknowledging that restoration can be motivated by — and designed to meet — different needs. “When you talk about conservation or restoration, the first question has to be restoration by whom, for whom?” says Daniel Janzen, a biologist at the University of Pennsylvania.
paragraphs.translationZh: 由于还有大量研究要做，该领域的领导者一直在进行一些自我反省，并承认恢复可以由不同的需求驱动并旨在满足不同的需求。 “当你谈论保护或恢复时，第一个问题必须是由谁恢复、为谁恢复？”宾夕法尼亚大学生物学家丹尼尔·詹森 (Daniel Janzen) 说道。

paragraphs.sourceText: The question can have more than one answer. Much of the global funding for restoration is dedicated to developing it as a tool to mitigate climate change, notes restoration ecologist Pedro Brancalion. “But if you ask a farmer in Brazil if he or she is concerned about climate change, they would say, ‘No, I am concerned about water,’ ” he says. Their interests as stewards of the land need to be better integrated with those who have the money to support restoration.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这个问题可以有多个答案。恢复生态学家 Pedro Brancalion 指出，全球恢复资金的大部分都致力于将其开发为缓解气候变化的工具。 “但如果你问巴西农民是否担心气候变化，他们会说，‘不，我担心水，’”他说。他们作为土地管理者的利益需要与那些有钱支持恢复的人更好地结合起来。

paragraphs.sourceText: That has been the strongest lesson of all for forest ecologist Robin Chazdon. Restoration is about more than what gets planted in the ground, she says. “Yes, it’s about forests, but it’s really about people. They are the agents of restoration.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 对于森林生态学家罗宾·查兹登来说，这是最深刻的教训。她说，恢复不仅仅是在地里种植什么。 “是的，这与森林有关，但实际上与人有关。他们是恢复的推动者。”

paragraphs.sourceText: Translate the following text into Chinese. Write your translation on the ANSWER SHEET. (15 points)
paragraphs.translationZh: 将下列文字翻译成中文。将您的翻译写在答题卡上。 （15分）

paragraphs.sourceText: The influence of wearables on psychology refers to how the clothes we wear affect our thoughts, feelings, and behaviors. Clothing is not just about covering our bodies; it plays a significant role in shaping our self-perception and interactions with others.
paragraphs.translationZh: 可穿戴设备对心理学的影响是指我们穿的衣服如何影响我们的思想、感受和行为。衣服不仅仅是为了遮盖我们的身体，更是为了遮盖我们的身体。它在塑造我们的自我认知和与他人的互动方面发挥着重要作用。

paragraphs.sourceText: One aspect of this influence is self-expression. The clothes we choose can reflect our personality, mood, and identity. Whether we opt for bold, colorful outfits or prefer more understated styles, our dress choices convey messages about who we are and how we want to be perceived.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种影响的一方面是自我表达。我们选择的衣服可以反映我们的个性、心情和身份。无论我们选择大胆、色彩缤纷的服装还是更喜欢低调的风格，我们的着装选择都传达了关于我们是谁以及我们希望如何被感知的信息。

paragraphs.sourceText: Additionally, clothing can impact our confidence levels. When we wear clothes that make us feel comfortable and confident, it can positively affect our self-esteem and overall mood.
paragraphs.translationZh: 此外，服装也会影响我们的信心水平。当我们穿着让我们感到舒适和自信的衣服时，它可以积极影响我们的自尊和整体情绪。

paragraphs.sourceText: Moreover, cultural and societal influences play a significant role in shaping our dress choices. Different cultures have their norms and expectations regarding dress, which can influence the types of clothing people wear and the meanings attributed to them.
paragraphs.translationZh: 此外，文化和社会影响在塑造我们的着装选择方面发挥着重要作用。不同的文化对着装有不同的规范和期望，这会影响人们穿着的服装类型及其赋予的含义。
